settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: DefaultHostnameVerifier (the default, non-deprecated implementation) does not call getDNSSubjectAlts; it uses its own private getSubjectAltNames and evaluates subjectAlts directly, so the default HttpClient path is unaffected.
Inside this repository getDNSSubjectAlts has no internal caller, so no in-repo runtime path demonstrates the faulty return value being consumed.
The class and its API are marked @Deprecated in favor of javax.net.ssl.HostnameVerifier/DefaultHostnameVerifier, reducing likelihood of use in current code.
candidates.description: In httpclient/src/main/java/org/apache/http/conn/ssl/AbstractVerifier.java, getDNSSubjectAlts(X509Certificate) collects DNS subject alternative names into dnsAlts and then returns `dnsAlts.isEmpty() ? dnsAlts.toArray(new String[dnsAlts.size()]) : null`. The ternary is inverted: when dnsAlts is non-empty (the normal success case) it returns null; when it is empty it returns a zero-length array. The declared contract (javadoc: 'Array of SubjectALT DNS names stored in the certificate') is therefore violated, and any caller that relies on this method to obtain SAN DNS names will receive null and may skip SAN-based verification, treating it as 'no SANs present'. The method is public static and part of the deprecated X509HostnameVerifier/AbstractVerifier API; the class-level javadoc marks the whole class deprecated in favor of DefaultHostnameVerifier. The trusted DefaultHostnameVerifier does not call this method (it uses its own getSubjectAltNames), so the practical impact depends on external code that still consumes AbstractVerifier. This is a logic/API-contract defect with potential security relevance when the returned value gates hostname checks; it is reported as a candidate, not a confirmed exploitable bypass.
missing_evidence: No in-repo caller of getDNSSubjectAlts showing that a null return leads to skipped SAN verification.
No test asserting the expected non-null return for a certificate with DNS SANs.
No evidence that any default HttpClient configuration invokes this deprecated code path.
preconditions: Code (in a consumer of the library, or legacy internal code) calls AbstractVerifier#getDNSSubjectAlts(cert) to enumerate certificate DNS subject alternative names and treats a null result as 'no SAN entries' / falls back to CN-only matching.
The legacy deprecated X509HostnameVerifier code path is in use rather than the default DefaultHostnameVerifier.
candidates.title: Deprecated AbstractVerifier#getDNSSubjectAlts returns null on the success path due to inverted ternary (always yields no SANs)
